en: Salutations to the illustrious Rāmānuja.

He who, out of delusion regarding the golden splendor of the two lotus feet of the Imperishable Lord, always regarded all other things as mere straw— of this our guru, the Blessed One, who is a singular ocean of compassion;
I take refuge at the feet of Rāmānuja.
Day and night I worship the noble Rāmānuja, the crest-jewel of the noble ones, who is a golden casket for the camphor of the Vedānta.
The Dialogue between Śrī Raṅganāyikā and Rāmānuja.

Śrī Rāmānuja [meditated upon] the Blessed Goddess, whose abode is the lotus grove, who possesses an infinite multitude of countless auspicious qualities— such as essential nature, form, attributes, majesty, sovereignty, and character— which are concordant with the will of the Lord Nārāyaṇa and are characterized by an unsurpassed excellence beyond measure.

I, having no other refuge, take refuge in Śrī, the Goddess who is eternally inseparable [from Him], the irreproachable divine queen of the God of gods, the mother of the entire universe, my own mother, the protector of the helpless.
[It is] produced by the experience of the Blessed One— [an experience] which is ultimate, characterized by exclusive and absolute supreme devotion,
performed through the highest devotion, complete, uninterrupted, eternal, most lucid, having no other purpose,
and consisting of an infinite and unsurpassed love; [and it is] caused by an infinite and unsurpassed joy born from that experience of the Blessed One.

May my ultimate refuge in the lotus feet of the Blessed Lord— characterized by the singular delight in serving all that remains [to be served] in every possible state, and undertaken with the expectation of attaining eternal service— be established according to reality and remain uninterrupted for me.
May the illustrious Raṅganāyikā be yours; through her alone shall everything be accomplished.
The Dialogue between Śrī Raṅganātha and Rāmānuja.
Śrī Rāmānuja [praises] Him who is the sole repository of all auspicious attributes, the adversary of everything that is to be avoided; who is distinct from all things other than Himself;
whose singular nature consists of infinite and manifold bliss; and who possesses a single, inconceivable, divine, and wonderful form that is perfectly suited to His own will.
O Divine Form, treasure-house of infinite qualities such as eternal, irreproachable, unsurpassed brilliance, beauty, fragrance, delicacy, loveliness, and youth;
O You who possess natural, limitless, and supreme strength, sovereignty, valor, power, splendor, and gentleness!

O Great Ocean of the vast multitude of countless auspicious qualities, such as affection, gentleness, straightforwardness, friendliness, equanimity, compassion, sweetness, profundity, magnanimity, cleverness, steadfastness, fortitude, heroism, prowess, having true desires, having true resolves, skillfulness, and the state of being accomplished!

It is characterized by various and manifold wonders appropriate to itself, eternally marvelous, perpetual, irreproachable, and unsurpassed fragrance; it possesses unsurpassed pleasant touch and unsurpassed brilliance; and it is adorned with a crown, a tiara, a crest-jewel, shark-shaped earrings, neck-ornaments, necklaces, armlets, bracelets, the Śrīvatsa mark, the Kaustubha gem, and strings of pearls.

O You who wear a waistband, yellow garments, a girdle-string, anklets, and countless other divine ornaments; O You whose inconceivable power is commensurate with Yourself; O You who possess the conch, discus, mace, sword, Śārṅga bow, and other innumerable, eternal, faultless, and unsurpassed divine weapons that bestow auspiciousness!

O Beloved of the Glory of the multitude of countless, excellent, and boundlessly superior auspicious qualities— such as Your own desired, eternal, and irreproachable essential nature, form, attributes, majesty, sovereignty, and character!
O Leader of the Earth and the World, who are such as this!

O You whose pair of feet is served by an infinite multitude of various attendants and female servants, headed by Śeṣa, Śeṣāśana, and Garuḍa; O You who act according to Your own will, whose nature is distinguished by the states of abiding and acting, whose sole delight is in the state of being the Remainder of all that remains, and who possess an infinite collection of auspicious qualities such as eternal, blameless, unsurpassed sovereignty and power!

O Lord of Śrī Vaikuṇṭha! You whose essential nature and character are beyond the comprehension of the speech and mind of the supreme yogis; you who are enriched with various, diverse, and infinite objects of enjoyment, instruments of enjoyment, and places of enjoyment according to Your own will; you who possess infinite wonders and infinite great majesty; you who are infinite in measure, eternal, faultless, and unsurpassed!

O Thou whose play consists in the arising, manifestation, and dissolution of the entire universe— which conforms to Thy own volition, whose nature, subsistence, and activity consist solely in being subordinate to Thee, and which takes the form of the infinite, diverse, and manifold categories of enjoyers, objects of enjoyment, instruments of enjoyment, and places of enjoyment, comprising Prakṛti, Puruṣa, and Kāla!
O Satyakāma! O Satyasaṅkalpa! O You who have become the Supreme Brahman! O Puruṣottama! O Mahāvibhūti! O Śrīman!
O Nārāyaṇa! O Lord of Vaikuṇṭha!
O Great Ocean of boundless compassion, virtuous conduct, affection, generosity, sovereignty, and beauty!

O You who have not disregarded distinctions, O refuge of the entire world! O remover of the distress of those who bow before You! O sole ocean of affection for those who take shelter in You! O You whose true nature as the reality of all classes of beings is known incessantly! O You who are ever intent on governing the entirety of all moving and non-moving beings! O You who are the sovereign Lord of all sentient and insentient entities!

O support of the entire universe! O Lord of the whole world! O Lord of us! O You whose desires are true! O You whose resolves are true! O You who are distinct from all else! O fulfiller of the needs of those who seek You! O friend in adversity! O glorious Nārāyaṇa! O refuge of the refugeless! Having no other refuge, I take shelter in Your pair of lotus feet.
In this regard, two things are to be considered:
"Father, mother, wife, sons, kinsmen, friends, teachers,
jewels, wealth, grain, fields, and houses."
"Having renounced all phenomena and all worldly desires along with their expressions, O All-pervading Lord, I have gone for refuge to you, whose feet stride across the worlds.
You alone are my mother and you alone are my father; you alone are my kinsman and you alone are my teacher."
You alone are my knowledge, you alone are my wealth, and you alone are everything to me, O God of gods.
"You are the Father of this world of the moving and the unmoving; you are its worshipful one, its teacher, and its greatest preceptor.

There is no one equal to you—how then could there be anyone superior? Even among those in the three worlds who possess incomparable power, O Lord of matchless majesty! Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I seek to propitiate you, the adorable Lord."
"O Lord, just as a father forgives his son, a friend his friend, or a lover his beloved, you ought to forgive [me].

[Forgive] the various and infinite transgressions committed through mind, speech, and body since beginningless time— consisting of performing what should not be done, failing to do what should be done, offenses against the Blessed One, offenses against the devotees, and other forms of intolerable offenses."
Forgive all of them without exception— those who have begun their actions, those who have not begun their actions, those already done, those being done, and those yet to be done.
[Forgive] the delusion proceeding from beginningless time, which concerns the self and concerns the entire world.
And forgive all conduct contrary to the right path, pertaining to every object, whether occurring even now, or that which has occurred in the past, or that which will occur in the future.

The divine Māyā, composed of the qualities (guṇas), which has proceeded from the stream of my beginningless karma; which causes the concealment of the true nature of the Lord; which generates perverse notions; which produces the perception of objects as things to be enjoyed; and which exists in the form of the body and senses, as objects of enjoyment, and in a subtle state.
"Save me who says, 'I have become a slave; I have come for refuge; I am your slave.
Among them, one who is constantly disciplined and possesses single-minded devotion is distinguished."
For I am exceedingly dear to the one who has no other, and he is dear to me.

All these [devotees] are indeed noble; yet it is my view that the self alone is [the most noble]. For he who is disciplined in mind, being firmly established in Me, attains Me alone as the unsurpassed goal.
"Having attained Me after many births, he who realizes 'Vāsudeva is everything' takes refuge in Me; such a great-souled one is very rare."
Therefore, make me one who does not take pride in what has been declared in these three verses:
"That Supreme Person, O Pārtha, is attainable by unswerving devotion," "He can be attained by unswerving devotion," and "He attains supreme devotion unto Me."

Thus, make me one endowed with the supreme devotion arising from the three stations; make me one whose sole nature is the supreme devotion that is beyond even the highest [levels] of supreme devotion;
[make me] completely full, uninterrupted, eternal, and most pure, produced by supreme devotion, beyond the highest, and supreme devotion.

May I be an eternal servant whose sole purpose is nothing other than the experience of the Blessed One, who is the infinitely unsurpassed beloved; and may I be one whose nature consists solely in being the servant of all things in every state of existence, brought about by the infinitely unsurpassed love born from such an experience of the Blessed One.
Śrī Raṅganātha,
though devoid of all the means necessary for attaining such service to me as described above,
though overwhelmed by endless sins that oppose it, and though possessed of endless offenses against me— [remains so].

Even though I am possessed of my own transgressions; even though I am possessed of endless and unbearable transgressions; even though my very nature is deluded by beginningless false egoism which serves as the cause of these [transgressions]; even though I am bound by beginningless contrary latent impressions (vāsanā) which serve as both the cause and the effect of these two; and even though I am bound to a specific material nature (prakṛti) corresponding to this [state].
Rooted in this [ignorance], there arises the experience of internal, external, and celestial pleasure, pain, their causes,

and other objects of indifference; this consists of the contraction of the mind, which— though obstructed by obstacles to supreme devotion— is characterized by exclusive and absolute supreme devotion to the pair of my lotus-like feet.

By whatever means possible, you are a speaker of duality; yet, solely through my compassion, [you shall become] one whose obstacles to supreme devotion— consisting of exclusive and absolute devotion to my pair of lotus feet, which have utterly destroyed all causes [of bondage]— have been removed, and who has attained my grace regarding that very pair of my lotus feet, characterized by exclusive and absolute [devotion].

Supreme devotion (*paramabhakti*) is that which, through my grace alone, has directly realized the full extent of my essential nature, form, qualities, manifestations, and the instruments of my divine play as they truly exist; it is the state in which my subordination is directly established, whose very essence and nature consist solely in the relish of being my servant; it is the exclusive experience of me and the singular love for serving me.

May you become my eternal servant— your experience of me being complete, uninterrupted, constant, most vivid, having no other purpose, and characterized by an infinite and unsurpassed love; and you, whose form consists solely in the delight of being the servant of all things in every state, brought about by the infinite and unsurpassed joy generated from such an experience of me.
You have become thus:
free from even the scent of internal, external, or celestial suffering and obstacles;
you shall always speak in this manner, accompanied by the constant contemplation of the meaning of the two [mantras], until the fall of this very body here in Śrīraṅgam.
Enjoy happiness.
At the moment of the body's fall, however, through my grace alone, he became fully awakened; gazing only upon me,

with his former impressions and aspirations unimpaired, he effortlessly cast off this material nature in its gross and subtle forms— like a worn-out garment— and immediately attained the pair of my lotus feet, obtained by my favor.

You are my experience— exclusive, absolute, characterized by supreme devotion, performed with the highest reverence, complete, uninterrupted, eternal, most lucid, having no other purpose, and beloved beyond all measure; and you are that which is produced by such an experience of mine, brought about by the joy that is limitless and unsurpassed, and appropriate for every state of being.
You shall become an eternal servant, whose sole delight is in the state of being the remainder of all that remains without exception.
O Mother, let there be no doubt in this matter:
"Never before have I spoken a falsehood, nor shall I ever speak one.
"Rāma does not speak twice."
"To one who has surrendered but once, who entreats me saying 'I am yours,' I grant fearlessness from all beings; this is my vow. "Abandoning all duties, come to Me alone for refuge."
"I shall liberate you from all evils; do not grieve"—thus indeed was it said by me.
Therefore, being free from doubt regarding the attainment of the vision of my true nature, remain in happiness.
May mindfulness of performing service unto You arise at the time of my end;
O Blessed One, grant that this very practice be accomplished for me today.
Thus ends the *Śaraṇāgatigadya* within the *Gadyatraya-prabandha* composed by the venerable Bhagavad Rāmānuja. May all be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
